results.question: How do I avoid contractor scams after a flood?
results.answer:
To avoid contractor scams after a flood, do not pay a contractor in full upfront or in cash, get the offer in writing, and report suspected fraud or price gouging to (800) 621-0508 [1]. The Texas Attorney General warns that some contractors take upfront payment after a disaster and then fail to do the work [1].

results.question: What FEMA flood zone am I in and what does it mean?
results.answer:
Your location is in FEMA flood zone AE, which is a Special Flood Hazard Area [1]. This designation means that flood insurance is typically required if you have a federally backed mortgage [1]. 

However, being in a flood zone is only one input for assessing your risk [2]. "Not in a flood zone" is considered a dangerous misnomer, as flooding can also occur due to overloaded storm drains, roadside ditches, or sheet flow [3][4]. Historically, the majority of flood-related fatalities have occurred outside of designated 100- and 500-year flood hazard areas, with only 22% of Harris County deaths occurring inside the 100-year zone [5]. Additionally, records indicate that this specific location flooded during Hurricane Harvey [6]. You should consider flood insurance regardless of your zone, check your ground elevation, and ask neighbors about past flooding [2]. As of 6:50 AM CDT, there are no active alerts for your area [7].
Not official guidance. In danger, call 911.

results.question: Is flood insurance worth it if I rent an apartment?
results.answer:
Most renters insurance does not cover flood damage [1]. Under Texas Property Code 92.0135, landlords must provide written notice regarding whether a dwelling is in a 100-year floodplain, but homes outside of these areas can still flood [1]. Until that effective date, you generally have no flood coverage, though exceptions exist for policies required by a mortgage [2].

results.question: How long is the waiting period for flood insurance?
results.answer:
Flood insurance from the NFIP usually has a 30-day waiting period [1] (a few exceptions exist, e.g. buying with a mortgage; ask your agent). If you buy a policy today (2026-10-11), coverage generally starts 2026-11-10; until then you have no flood coverage. That is before hurricane season ends (2026-11-30). Buy before a storm is forecast.

results.question: ¿Cuánto tiempo de espera tiene el seguro contra inundaciones?
results.answer:
El seguro de inundación del NFIP normalmente tiene un período de espera de 30 días [1] (hay algunas excepciones, p. ej. al comprar con una hipoteca; pregunte a su agente). Si compra una póliza hoy (2026-10-11), la cobertura generalmente empieza el 2026-11-10; hasta entonces no tiene cobertura. Eso es antes de que termine la temporada de huracanes (2026-11-30). Compre antes de que se pronostique una tormenta.
Esto no es una guía oficial. En una emergencia, llame al 911.
